//: Who may touch what, written down BEFORE anyone starts. Read docs/parallel-dev.md first, then BOTH briefs: docs/specs/unipile-rooms-and-booking.md and docs/specs/adgrant-and-dev-agents.md. THIS IS PROGRAMME THREE, second half. Its first five parcels are landed and are kept in docs/parcels-programme-3-landed.json; programme two's thirteen are in docs/parcels-programme-2.json and programme one's nineteen in docs/parcels-programme-1.json. None of those three files is for running. Ownership freed by a retired parcel is reused here on purpose: adgrant-site inherits the AdGrant tree from adgrant-front, and booking-picker inherits the dialog from booking-dialog.
//brief: Two briefs, and a parcel reads the one its prompt names. unipile-rooms-and-booking.md carries the Unipile contract, the identity decisions and the rule that every inbound message is checked for who it is from, who it is to and which chat it is in. adgrant-and-dev-agents.md carries adgrant.ai's own content API, the six factual defects in the material being carried over, the split between generating a structure and uploading it, and the answer to the owner's question about per-agent limits. An agent that starts from a paraphrase instead will rebuild something that already exists or ship something that is wrong.
//seams: Files everything needs. A parcel may ADD up to three lines to one of these and delete none, and must declare which lines up front. Two one-line additions merge by keeping both; two thirty-line edits merge into something nobody can verify. THREE STATED EXCEPTIONS, carried over because the three-line grammar would make them unusable: scripts/build-kb.ts admits one appended Corpus const plus its name on the CORPORA line, shared/roster.ts admits one whole appended agent entry, and client/src/components/site/doors/bodies.tsx admits one door-to-body entry. All three are appends at the end of a list, which is the shape that merges. A FOURTH, added for programme three: shared/schema.ts admits one re-export line. A new table is fifteen lines and the seam allows three, so a parcel that needs a table writes it in its OWN file and re-exports it from the schema - drizzle-kit follows the export, and one line merges where fifteen do not.
//frozen: Nobody edits these during a parallel run. A change here invalidates every parcel at once. Programme three has one consequence worth stating: client/index.html carries the one <head> this application serves, so a second site on a second host cannot have its own title and meta without editing a frozen file. That is why adgrant-front builds a route tree and not a second host - the host switch is owner work, done when no wave is running.
//alone: Parcels marked runAlone touch the room, the panel or the shell - everything reads those, and two agents in them at once produce a merge nobody can check. One agent, let it finish, then start the others.
//order: The waves are in scripts/build-prompts.mjs and check-parcels.mjs reads them back. Programme three's ordering is a dependency chain, not a preference, and it has three links. (1) unipile-core is wave one ALONE because four parcels import its client; a parcel that writes its own Unipile client because the shared one did not exist yet is four incompatible error mappers. (2) booking-server and booking-dialog are the same wave and build to the request and response shapes fixed in the brief's section 3 - that is what fixing them in writing was for. (3) room-identity precedes login-create-room, because the claim dialog the site's new menu opens is the one room-identity builds. Beyond the chain, one standing rule: AT MOST ONE PARCEL PER WAVE MAY TOUCH server/routes.ts. Three parcels here need a route, and they are in three different waves for that reason alone.

server/routes.ts: the booking routes, pointed at the new calendar client
package.json: a Google auth dependency, if one is genuinely needed

calendar-direct.why: The booking calendar is the only thing left that a third party stands between us and, and that third party's account ids were in the source of a repository that is going public. A service account with the calendar shared to it needs no consent screen, no verification, no refresh token, and no vendor.
calendar-direct.done: BOOKINGS TALK TO GOOGLE CALENDAR DIRECTLY, THROUGH A SERVICE ACCOUNT. (1) THE MECHANISM, and it is chosen because it avoids three things: a service account authenticates with its own key, and the owner SHARES his calendar with that account's address with permission to make changes. No OAuth consent screen, so no sensitive-scope verification and no demo video; no refresh token to store; no vendor. The key is one environment variable holding the service account JSON, and .env.example says what breaks without it and, in one line each, the two steps in Google Cloud and in Google Calendar that a person has to do by hand. (2) EVERYTHING THE BOOKING ALREADY DOES KEEPS WORKING, and there are tests for all of it: the free/busy of OUR calendar that builds the slot grid, creating the event, deleting it on cancel, moving it on reschedule, the Meet link, the invite to an address, and the 45-second cache. Read server/booking/slots.ts and calendar.ts before you write: the behaviour is specified by their tests, and those tests are the contract, not the vendor. (3) OUR OWN AVAILABILITY CAN NOW USE freeBusy.query RATHER THAN LISTING EVENTS. Listing events was a workaround for a connector with no free/busy endpoint; reading busy ranges is narrower, faster and does not bring titles and guests into this process at all. If anything genuinely needs an event's own fields, say in a comment which and why. (4) NOTHING IS WRITTEN INTO ANYBODY ELSE'S CALENDAR. One calendar, the one shared with the service account. (5) THE VISITOR'S OWN CALENDAR IS NOT YOURS TO TOUCH: server/booking/freebusy.ts is a different app, a different grant and a different person, and it stays exactly as it is. WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: the slot grid's shape on the wire, the booking codes, the return links, and the popup. A person with a booking made yesterday must still be able to open, change and cancel it.

server/routes.ts: the inbound webhook and the WhatsApp routes, pointed at the new interface
shared/api.ts: whatever the panel learns about WhatsApp, if it changes at all

whatsapp-waha.why: WhatsApp on top-rated.team and adgrant.ai keeps working exactly as it does — the same number, the same account, the same bindings. What changes is that the repository stops naming the hosted service those two use, and describes WAHA instead, because WAHA is the only thing a fork or a white-label partner can actually run.
whatsapp-waha.done: ONE WHATSAPP INTERFACE, TWO TRANSPORTS BEHIND IT, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS ON GIT BY NAME. (1) THE INTERFACE, in server/whatsapp/: send a message to a chat, parse an inbound body, tell me our own number, tell me whether the account is alive. Everything above it — room sign-in, the booking proof, the confirmation reply, the QR probe — talks to THAT and to nothing else. server/waha.ts currently asks the hosted service for our own number; after this it asks the interface. (2) WAHA IS THE DEFAULT AND THE ONLY ONE DOCUMENTED. server/bridge/waha.ts already sends and already parses; make it the interface's WAHA transport rather than writing a second client. .env.example, README.md and docs/specs/whatsapp.md describe WAHA and nothing else, and docs/specs/whatsapp.md carries the few lines a fork needs: run WAHA, pair your number, set these variables, point the webhook here. That is the ONLY WhatsApp instruction a partner ever gets. (3) THE OTHER TRANSPORT IS A GENERIC HOSTED-API ADAPTER, server/whatsapp/hosted.ts, and it names no vendor. Its base URL, its auth header, its account ids and its webhook secret all come from the environment — they are values on a deployment, not strings in a repository. Where a request or response shape is specific to the service we happen to use, handle it there and say what the shape is, not whose it is. THIS IS NOT DECEPTION AND MUST NOT BECOME IT: the file is honestly a generic adapter, and a comment at its head says so and says that the vendor-specific transcript lives in private/ for whoever maintains it. (4) THE HOUSE DEPLOYMENT DOES NOT CHANGE ITS BEHAVIOUR. Same number, same account, same peppered chat-id hashes, so every existing binding still resolves — selecting the transport is reading the environment, not a migration. If both are configured, the hosted one wins on a house host and WAHA everywhere else; write that rule down where a person will find it. (5) THE SEVEN INBOUND CHECKS SURVIVE INTACT — who it is from, who it is to, which chat it is in, is it our own echo, is it a group, has the code expired, is the account ours — for BOTH transports, with their tests. They are the reason nobody has proved a room they do not own, and a check dropped because a webhook spells a field differently is the bug this parcel exists to avoid. (6) THE VENDOR LEAVES THE REPOSITORY: docs/specs/unipile-rooms-and-booking.md goes, its transport-neutral content — the seven checks, the four decisions, the booking shapes — reappearing in docs/specs/whatsapp.md and docs/specs/booking.md written without a vendor in them, and its endpoint transcript moving to private/, which is already gitignored and already where things that must not be published live. Then no UNIPILE_ name, no vendor name, in any tracked file. WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE: WhatsApp stays house-only where shared/operator.ts says so, the sign-in code is still spent on first use, no phone number is ever stored or logged, and the QR still renders on a white plate and not at all on a phone.
